markets._shape_anomaly_notes: unattended-ops: if >=shape_anomaly_min_sample markets were fetched and more than shape_anomaly_threshold of them are missing a required field, main.py aborts before scoring and alerts rather than processing what's likely a Kalshi API shape change as if it were real data.
markets._near_dated_notes: Supplements the events-catalog fetch (fetch_events -- which structurally never surfaces near-dated markets, confirmed 2026-08-01) with a direct /markets?max_close_ts=... fetch, filtered to exclude the KXMVE parlay flood. Feeds both the main scanner's short-horizon buckets and resolve_first.py's near-dated selector, which was previously starved (1 row logged in its whole history).
markets._prop_market_exclude_notes: backlog: prop-market-skill-filter. Ticker-prefix exclusion in core.scanner.filter_markets(), same mechanism as near_dated_exclude_prefixes/KXMVE. KXMLBMENTION ('what will the announcer say') markets have no real predictive skill ceiling the way a price/outcome market does, but are liquid enough to clear every other filter -- confirmed 2026-08-01: 10/36 near-dated markets sampled were this category and survived volume/OI/price/close-time filters cleanly. Conservative default (only the one category with concrete zero-skill-ceiling evidence); extend the list if other gimmick categories turn up.

scoring._repeat_dedup_notes: How long a ticker stays suppressed as a repeat (main.py's is_repeat tagging, core.logger.get_recent_tickers) before a fresh flag logs as a brand-new signal row. Widened 7 -> 30 (2026-08-20) after finding a genuine same-market direction flip (KXMLBDEBUT-KANDERSON-26NOV01: NO on 2026-06-29, YES on 2026-07-06, 8 days apart -- just outside the old 7-day window) that will resolve as one win and one loss for the same underlying event by construction, and a separate ticker with 3 resolved rows all agreeing -- both inflate resolved_count (every locked backlog item's gate) with non-independent samples. 30 days doesn't eliminate re-flagging on long-dated markets, just meaningfully reduces near-term whipsaws like the 8-day case. Distinct from resolve_first_dedup_days, an unrelated analysis/resolve_first.py setting.

accounts.watchlist_note: monthly_pnl values below are for human reference only (why each address was added). They are never used as a basis for signal decisions; all promotion requires passing _is_winner() against resolved positions.

blind_arm._blind_arm_notes: price-blind-arm: when enabled, samples up to sample_size markets per run (from those the anchored scorer already scored) and re-scores them with no market price shown and no price-anchoring instructions, via the metered Anthropic API (core.llm.score_blind_via_api, counts against llm.daily_cost_ceiling_usd). Results are logged to their own blind_scores DB table and never feed signal selection. Off by default because this spends real metered API cost on every run it fires, unlike the main scan (Pro subscription, no per-token bill) -- enable deliberately, not as a default-on side effect of an unrelated config change.

betting._betting_notes: min_ev_pct_of_unit was lowered from 0.50 to 0.25 (goal 4d). Historical check showed 0.50 passed only ~6.5% of logged signals. Revisit once n>=20 resolved signals exist so the floor can be grounded in observed edge decay. dynamic_sizing_enabled (2026-07-27) is a human opt-in for confidence-weighted stake sizing (core/sizing.py) -- stays fully inert until resolved_count>=30 AND resolved_count_per_category_max>=15 (mirrors auto-calibration-loop's own trigger), regardless of this flag.

report._base_url_notes: GOAL_phase2-6_decisions.md Decision 3: the single hosting switch for every cross-page link the subscriber digest emits (currently just the Track Record link). Empty string (default) keeps the current relative-path behavior for local preview (harness writes both HTML files to the same folder). Once real hosting/email delivery exists, set this to that host's base URL (e.g. "https://leviathan.example.com") and every such link becomes absolute -- one config change, no code change.

llm._llm_notes: daily_cost_ceiling_usd (goal llm-cost-ceiling) only applies to real metered spend via score_via_api/probe_via_api (core/llm.py) -- the main scan runs backend=cli against the Pro subscription with no per-token bill, so this ceiling protects research probes, eval re-scoring, and the future replay-runner, which will call the API path at volume. $20/day is a starting guess, not a measured figure; revisit once replay-runner exists and real per-market API cost is observed. api_spend_authorized is a hard runtime gate on every core.llm metered function -- leave false; only flip true for a specific, time-boxed, explicitly-authorized session, then flip back.

monday._monday_notes: scripts/monday_sync.py, Phases 0-4 (docs/monday_sync_discovery.md, docs/monday_sync_runbook.md). backlog.json stays the source of truth; monday is a view + progress log, one-way push in v1. MONDAY_API_TOKEN lives in .env only, never here. These ids are resolved live at runtime (get_board_schema()) and re-written into the real config.json on every --phase1/--phase2/--phase3 run -- values here are just the last-known-good snapshot for reference. board_id/workspace_id/group ids/column ids are not secrets (only the API token is); if the board is ever recreated these will need re-resolving, which --phase1 does automatically. dry_run_default (actually read by the script, not just documented) governs a BARE invocation with neither --dry-run nor --live -- the scheduled task always passes --live explicitly and never depends on this value, so changing it only affects manual ad-hoc runs at a clean prompt.
